title: POC Weekly Sync - Havenridge Bench Contrast
summary: Weekly POC sync reviewing bench results vs current vendor. Redwood showed improved p50/p95 and tail reductions under typical traffic patterns; customers raised questions about VPC/KMS, SOC2 artifacts, and dedicated slot commitments. Agreed to run a 1hr load test at production-like concurrency and send security pack + pricing for a 3 month pilot. Decision target end of August.
action_items: Samantha Ortiz: Share security questionnaire + SOC2 report by 2026-08-10
Daniel Cho: Schedule 1hr load test in Redwood sandbox and provide runbook by 2026-08-12
Priya Menon: Provide production traffic trace and p99 SLOs by 2026-08-11
next_steps: Redwood to run 1hr load test with Havenridge trace (schedule week of Aug 10)
Send dedicated slot pricing + reserve option for pilot
Security deep-dive call if questions remain after docs reviewed
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-07
Start: 10:30 AM PT
Duration: ~58 minutes
Attendees: Samantha Ortiz, Daniel Cho, Marcos Li - Redwood; Priya Menon, James Carter, Luca Moretti, Ellen Park - Havenridge

Summary (auto): weekly POC bench readout, compare to incumbent baseline, triage latency tail and throughput routing behavior.

[00:00] Samantha Ortiz: hey everyone, thanks for hopping on, quick roll call?
[00:08] Priya Menon: priya here, james and luca and ellen on our side
[00:12] James Carter: yep james here, infra
[00:14] Daniel Cho: daniel from redwood, se
[00:16] Samantha Ortiz: cool, agenda — results walk, routing playbook, actions. we'll start with marcos on the bench summary
[00:25] Marcos Li: alright so we ran the head-to-head with your sample trace, baseline provider was IncumbentCloud with their small-replicated endpoint. average payloads were 450 tokens, convo style. our measured p50 was ~120ms, p95 310ms, p99 420ms in the earlier runs but after enabling kv-prefix caching and adaptive batching p99 dropped to ~265ms, p95 ~190ms. throughput sustained at 360 rps on the dedicated test slot vs baseline 220 rps
[01:05] Priya Menon: just to confirm those are token-latencies end-to-end or server-side?
[01:10] Marcos Li: good call — numbers are server-side generation time measured at the agent, not including network egress; when we add a 30-40ms network delta your end-to-end was estimated at p95 ~230ms vs incumbent ~380ms
[01:28] Luca Moretti: the p99 reduction looks promising. what's the quant config? are you using int8 or 4-bit?
[01:34] Daniel Cho: we used our mixed quant profile — embedding & attn kernels in 4-bit for some layers and int8 for others. the key was kernel selection + KV cache so repeat prefixes are cheap. we can switch to full int8 for even lower memory but might change quality a smidge, so we'd test against your eval set
[02:00] Ellen Park: any stability issues under 75% load? our production peaks are spiky, sudden bursts
[02:06] Marcos Li: no crashes in our runs; we used burst autoscale and a route-fallback to a slightly slower but cheaper model variant to keep requests healthy when slots saturated. tail increased briefly during spikes but routing TTL and canary thresholds kept error rate under 0.5%
[02:28] Priya Menon: interesting — can you explain the routing/fallback logic again, and how it affects latency SLO?
[02:34] Daniel Cho: sure — policy is layered: prefer low-latency instances in primary region, if queue depth > threshold or p95 exceeds configured SLO then route to secondary warm pool or model variant. fallback decision is incremental to avoid oscillation, and we instrument token-level metrics so you can see unit-cost impact
[03:02] James Carter: we need that traceable audit for routing events; who touched what, why fallback happened. that's important for compliance
[03:11] Samantha Ortiz: yep we ship audit logs and can integrate with your SIEM; logs include route decisions, instance ids, model version, and decision rationale. we'll include sample log extract in the security pack
[03:26] Priya Menon: the SOC2 thing — do you have up-to-date report and KMS integration?
[03:31] Daniel Cho: we do, SOC2 type 2 current through June 2026. KMS: customer-managed keys supported via our VPC/private deploy and via our hosted offering with BYOK options. we'll share docs
[03:44] Luca Moretti: in the hosted flows, does the customer ever see plaintext model cache or any transcript artifacts?
[03:50] Marcos Li: no. KV cache is encrypted at rest; we support token scrubbing and retention policies. for private deployment you'd own the keys and logs
[03:59] Priya Menon: can we talk price v committed dedicated slots? our finance wants a predictable unit cost if we move to pilot
[04:05] Samantha Ortiz: absolutely — we have two options: reserved dedicated pool for consistent throughput (monthly commit) or a burstable dedicated slot where you pay baseline and overage. we'll send a tailored quote for a 3-month pilot and include cost per 1M tokens at your average 450-token payloads
[04:26] James Carter: on the perf numbers — what's the warmup behavior? we saw initial cold-start p99 spikes earlier in the test spreadsheet
[04:32] Daniel Cho: warm starts are handled by pre-warming and continuous batching; the coldest path (new model shard) can spike but we avoid it by pinning warm instances in the reserved pool and by using prefix cache to eliminate repeated context recompute
[04:46] Ellen Park: if we run the 1hr load test with our trace, what do you need from us?
[04:51] Marcos Li: just the trace and target concurrency profile, and optionally a subset of prompts for quality checks. we'll run in a sandbox dedicated slot and produce detailed token-level latency histograms and per-route cost estimates
[05:05] Priya Menon: one worry — model parity. we need parity on our in-house finetuned model behaviors, not just raw speed. how do we validate quality?
[05:13] Daniel Cho: we can run diff-evals using your eval prompts and the golden outputs. we'll run A/B at equal seeds and produce a summary of differences; if quantization introduces regressions we revert quant profile or change kernel map until quality is acceptable
[05:30] Samantha Ortiz: ok, let's triage a few anomalies from the spreadsheet — page 3 shows a throughput drop at 18:42 during a spike
[05:36] Marcos Li: that was due to one node hitting memory pressure because its quantized kernel didn't fit the batch size. we lowered batch upper bound and enabled spill-to-cpu which smoothed throughput at cost of ~12% higher latency for that node only
[05:54] Priya Menon: can you share the kernel mapping? the term you used, 'kv-prefix caching' — our notes earlier said 'prefix kvcache' — minor but we want consistent terms
[06:02] Daniel Cho: sorry for the transcribe goof. we call it 'prefix/KV cache' internally, it's basically cached key-value states for repeating prefixes to avoid recompute
[06:12] Luca Moretti: what's the expected unit cost reduction vs incumbent if you maintain those throughput numbers?
[06:18] Samantha Ortiz: rough math from our bench: unit token cost was ~0.62x of incumbent at your payload size — mostly from better batching and reduced tail which reduces wasted compute. we'll provide a detailed cost ladder in the quote
[06:31] James Carter: any network residency concerns? we need EU data residency for some clients, though our primary infra is US-based
[06:38] Marcos Li: we have region routing and can pin to EU data plane for specific tenants; private deploy supports on-prem or VPC egress controls for strict residency
[06:48] Ellen Park: SSO and RBAC — we need SAML + SCIM provisioning
[06:53] Daniel Cho: supported; RBAC maps to project and route-level roles. we'll attach an implementation doc
[07:00] Priya Menon: ok good. next — deep dive scheduling. we want the detailed routing and kill-switch demonstration before committing. can that be the security deep-dive?
[07:08] Samantha Ortiz: yes can do, daniel can demo the routing playbook and failover in a 45 minute session
[07:13] Daniel Cho: i'll prepare a scripted failover with metrics so you can see route shifts and logs
[07:19] Priya Menon: timeline — finance wants a go/no-go by Aug 28. does that align with your pilot delivery schedule?
[07:25] Samantha Ortiz: yes, if we run the load test next week and you review docs, we can have a pilots pricing and runbook by Aug 17 and then you can decide by Aug 28
[07:34] Luca Moretti: on the pricing, can you include committed three-month and month-to-month options?
[07:37] Samantha Ortiz: yep will do
[07:40] James Carter: one small ask — include sample audit log schema so our compliance team can map fields
[07:46] Marcos Li: will include sample snippet and a mapping table with field descriptions
[07:51] Priya Menon: ok that covers most, let's confirm action owners
[07:55] Samantha Ortiz: action items recap — (1) sam: security pack + SOC2 by Aug 10, (2) daniel: sandbox load test + runbook by Aug 12, (3) priya: supply trace and SLOs by Aug 11, (4) marcos: kernel mapping doc and audit sample by Aug 12
[08:18] Ellen Park: small clarif — will the logs include IPs or just instance ids?
[08:23] Daniel Cho: can redact IPs or include them depending on your privacy needs; we'll default to instance ids and decision tags
[08:30] Priya Menon: if the A/B eval shows minor diff, what's the rollback policy?
[08:33] Daniel Cho: immediate rollback to prior quant profile or model version; our rollout supports canary percentages and automatic rollback on quality regressions or increased error rates
[08:45] Samantha Ortiz: ok final recap: run load test week of Aug 10, send security pack and pricing, schedule routing demo during security deep-dive. decision target Aug 28. anything else?
[08:56] Luca Moretti: no, thanks all
[08:58] Samantha Ortiz: thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with artifacts

End of transcript.
crm_notes: POC is healthy; customer motivated by latency tail reduction and predictable cost. Primary blockers: SOC2 docs + final finance approval. Timing suggests potential pilot conversion if benchmarks hold in sandbox load test.
